nodes.description: Two families carry balanced translocations, t(8;12)(q13;p11.2) and t(4;12)(q13.2-13.3;p11.2), with breakpoints outside PTHLH. Neither disrupts the coding sequence; both lower PTHLH expression by breaking its regulatory landscape, including a long-range element on 12q that contacts PTHLH in cis over 24.4 Mb and SOX9 in trans and carries a long noncoding RNA. Patient fibroblasts differentiated into chondrogenic cells show reduced PTHLH and impaired chondrogenic differentiation, so the regulatory lesion converges on the same dosage reduction as the coding alleles.

nodes.description: PTHrP from the enamel epithelium (stellate reticulum) acts on PTH1R in the dental follicle, which then supports osteoclast formation and resorption of the bone over the crown. Evidence is from mice lacking PTHrP outside cartilage and from dental crypt cell culture; in patients the corresponding finding is delayed or failed eruption.

nodes.description: Heterozygous loss of PTHLH function. The allele spectrum is all loss-of-function: whole-gene and contiguous deletions, nonsense and frameshift variants, a nonstop extension, initiation-codon and signal-peptide variants (p.L15R impairs signal-peptide cleavage), and missense variants in the N-terminal PTH-like domain, of which L60P was shown to lose function in chicken micromass culture. That deletions and truncations give the same phenotype as the point mutations is the argument for haploinsufficiency. Duplications of PTHLH cause different disorders (enchondromatosis, acro-osteolysis, a combined type E/A1 osteochondroplasia) and are outside this entry.

nodes.description: The genetic counterpart of the human disorder: heterozygous loss of PTHrP. Normal at birth, with skeletal abnormalities developing postnatally while PTH and calcium stay normal.

In the growth plate, prehypertrophic chondrocytes secrete Indian hedgehog, which induces PTHrP in the periarticular perichondrium and resting chondrocytes; PTHrP acts through PTH1R on prehypertrophic chondrocytes to keep them proliferating and to delay hypertrophy. This negative feedback loop sets how long a chondrocyte column keeps growing. Mice heterozygous for a Pthrp null allele show that the loop is dosage-sensitive: they are normal at birth but develop bone abnormalities postnatally, while circulating PTH and calcium stay normal, which matches the normal mineral biochemistry of affected people.
